newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore property market crash unlikely - experts.
newsitem.headline: Singapore property market crash unlikely - experts.

text.p: Singapore's private property market is not going to crash, property experts were quoted as saying in the Sunday Times.
Singapore's share market took a hit last week, led by losses in the property index, after a real estate group predicted a collapse in the sector.

Speaking at a forum organised by the National University of Singapore (NUS), property consultants and real estate academics said a crash was unlikely due to the island state's stable economy and healthy demand from genuine home-buyers.
The slide in prices has been too small and gradual to cause a collapse, the newspaper quoted them as saying.
In the 12 months following the government's measures in May last year to cool excessive property speculation, prices have dropped 8.9 percent to late-1995 levels, they said.
The curbs included taxing property within three years of purchase and capping private housing loans to 80 percent of a property's value.
But the fall was slight compared to the price increases every year since 1993, said NUS lecturer Dr Yu Lai Boon.
Prices jumped 36 percent in 1993, soared 42 percent in 1994 and rose 10 percent in 1995, he said.
All speakers at the forum disagreed with last week's prediction of a property crash by the Real Estate Developers Association of Singapore (REDAS).
Dominated by big land developers, REDAS had appealed to the government to reduce its land sales to avoid a collapse in property prices.
"In the past, developers were used to enjoying supernormal profit," Yu said.
"I think (the) government should not accede too much to developers' request," he said.
